newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed unchanged after a quiet session on Wednesday, recovering from early weakness caused by lost confidence in the market's rally.
Dealers said yesterday's gains had been an overreaction, triggered by relief over the agreement between the German government and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of gold reserves.
"Today, it's purely technical trade. Only professionals are active at the moment, buying and selling small quantities," one dealer said.

Under the compromise reached yesterday, the German government will not benefit from the gold revaluation in 1997, forcing it to fill the budget gap -- and thereby qualify for a single European currency -- by other means.
Dutch bonds closed at a two week high on Tuesday, with market players jubilant over the compromise.
Today, the market ignored U.S. April factory orders which were above expectations.
Factory orders rose 1.2 percent in April, whereas economists had forecast an 0.8 percent rise. Factory orders for March were revised upward 0.3 percent to a 1.3 percent drop.
"What counts is the euro. France finally isn't that bad, and it seems Germany might solve its problems, although unemployment remains a black cloud over that country," one dealer said.
Dealers said players were uninspired as they were uncertain over the market's direction.
Trade was said to be relatively active in the very short segment, of bonds maturing in 2000, and in five-year bonds.
The 8.25 percent state bonds maturing in February 2002 ended one basis point lower at 114.43/53 bid/ask.
